questions.q: What is the main benefit of putting a message broker between two services?
o: The producer does not wait for the consumer to be running
Every call becomes synchronous and ordered
Retries are no longer needed anywhere
Messages are guaranteed never to repeat
questions.w: Producers and consumers can scale and fail independently, and the broker buffers bursts.

questions.q: What is the difference between a queue and a topic (publish/subscribe)?
o: A queue delivers each message to one consumer, a topic to every subscriber
A queue carries text while a topic carries binary data
A topic keeps messages forever while a queue keeps none
The two are the same thing under different names
questions.w: Queues share work between competing consumers. Topics broadcast events to independent subscribers, each with its own position or queue.

questions.q: Which delivery guarantee is the realistic default for most brokers?
o: At-least-once, so consumers must tolerate duplicates
Exactly-once end to end with no extra work
At-most-once with guaranteed delivery
Exactly-once for free between any two systems
questions.w: Acknowledge after processing and a crash causes redelivery. Make consumers idempotent, for example by tracking message ids.

questions.q: A consumer keeps failing on one malformed message. What stops it blocking the queue?
o: Retry a few times, then park it in a dead-letter queue
Retry for ever without waiting between the attempts
Delete the message silently so nobody ever sees it
Restart the broker every few minutes until it works
questions.w: A dead-letter queue parks poison messages for inspection and replay. Retries should use backoff.

questions.q: Why does Kafka guarantee ordering only within a partition?
o: Each partition is an ordered log read by one consumer in a group
Kafka sorts all messages by their timestamp
Every topic is limited to a single broker
The producer's clock enforces the ordering
questions.w: Use a key (for example the account id) so all related events go to the same partition and stay in order.

o: Slowing or limiting producers when consumers fall behind
Encrypting messages when the system is under load
Deleting the oldest messages first
Raising the replica count of the topic
questions.w: Without it queues grow without bound. Options include bounded queues, rate limits, pull-based consumption and scaling consumers.

questions.q: A service updates its database and then publishes an event. It crashes between the two steps. Which pattern solves this?
o: Transactional outbox: save the event in the same database transaction
Publish first and update the database a little afterwards
Use a much longer timeout on the publish call itself
Send the same event twice just to be on the safe side
questions.w: The two systems cannot share one transaction. The outbox makes the event part of the local commit and a relay publishes it, with at-least-once delivery.

questions.q: What is a consumer group in Kafka?
o: Consumers sharing a group id divide the topic's partitions
A set of brokers that hold replicas of a topic
A group of producers that write in order
A list of topic names a client may use
questions.w: Different groups each receive the full stream. Within one group each partition is read by only one member at a time.
